question: Should OpenClaw accept this external contributor's exact-head ACPX dependency graph bump to `acpx@0.12.0`, or require a maintainer/security-owned regeneration path?
rationale: The diff is coherent, but the package manifest, shrinkwrap, and root lockfile change executable ACP harness dependencies in an external PR, and repository automation is deliberately blocking that without explicit approval.

options.title: Approve exact head after proof
options.body: After reviewing the dependency delta and receiving OpenClaw ACP smoke proof, a repository admin or security owner approves the current head SHA for merge.

options.title: Regenerate on maintainer branch
options.body: A maintainer reproduces the same `acpx@0.12.0` bump and docs/runtime alignment on a trusted branch to avoid accepting an external dependency graph change.

options.title: Pause bundled consumption
options.body: Keep the upstream ACPX support external for now if maintainers do not want OpenClaw's bundled plugin to advertise `grok-build` yet.

recommendation.title: Approve exact head after proof
recommendation.body: After reviewing the dependency delta and receiving OpenClaw ACP smoke proof, a repository admin or security owner approves the current head SHA for merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest combined history across ACPX dependency ownership, process-lease runtime behavior, and release/security-sensitive dependency updates.
